model: Organic score = 100 x listed x findable x reach. listed: 1 live, 0.5 PR or submission pending, 0.2 blocked on a human step, 0 skipped/not published. findable for registry-backed surfaces is MEASURED: p(seen | query) = 0 if our LATEST (v0.2.0) row does not appear in the result list, else min(1, 10/rank); findable = mean of p over the 41 natural queries across all six servers' query_set (was 34 across four servers before expense-tracker and office-suite existed). Per-server organic = 100 x mean(p) over that server's own query set. 'Hosted endpoints' is a new surface: findable = share of the 41 query slots where the matched row is a v0.2.0 entry that carries a non-empty remotes[] (time-tracker, price-tracker and invoice publish remotes; spreadsheet and expense-tracker do not; office-suite has no row at all). fleet.fleet_score is a noisy-OR over the six per-server organic scores (100 x (1 - product(1 - p_i/100))), applied identically before and after so the two are comparable; the previously stored fleet_score (78) used an undocumented aggregation and is not reused here. Reach and 'listed' for non-registry surfaces remain estimates, called out below.

fleet.verdict: Two new servers arrived with v0.2.0: expense-tracker is live and already the fleet's strongest server (organic 66.7, on the back of 4 near-empty tokens including a rank-1-of-1 on 'mileage'); office-suite exists on disk but was never published and contributes exactly 0 everywhere it could otherwise help. remotes[] is live on 3 of 6 servers (time-tracker, price-tracker, invoice), which is what the new 'Hosted endpoints' surface measures (findable 0.317, score 15.9) -- spreadsheet and expense-tracker still ship stdio-only. Registry findable rose only slightly, 0.239 to 0.276, because office-suite added 2 unmatched tokens to the denominator at the same time expense-tracker added 4 matched ones; the fleet as a whole is stronger than the mean-findable number alone suggests, which is why fleet_score (noisy-OR across the six per-server organics) moved from a recomputed 70.6 to 90.1 -- adding one strong, findable server does more for 'is any of our servers reachable' than it does for the average reachability of an arbitrary token. Bing and DuckDuckGo indexation of mcp.zovo.one could not be measured via curl this run (Bing ignored the site: filter and served an unrelated fallback SERP; DDG served a CAPTCHA) -- that stays an open unknown, not a zero. The next lever is still not naming: publish office-suite, add remotes[] to the two stdio-only servers, and drive installs on surfaces that rank by installs (Smithery useCounts run from 19 to 56,138 among competitors we do not appear next to at all).
